IBEW.text:
**Trampin the IBEW Indoor Locals — Wednesday, September 30, 2026**

**LU-613 Atlanta, GA** is running heavy with 127 calls and nearly 1,000 hands on the board. Miller Electrical and Inglett & Stubbs are both deep into QTS Fayetteville data center work at **$42/hr**, posting identical calls for 79 and 67 JWs respectively. Straight-ahead conduit and cable tray. Book 1 is still hunting.

**LU-481 Indianapolis, IN** has 57 calls with tight hand count (161 deep), and one call—Ermco's Lilly LP1 Lebanon job—is sitting at **$58.70/hr** for temperature control work. Industrial Electric's Eli Lilly K153 gig on the Southside is new construction with an extensive background check bite. This board has velocity.

**LU-545 St. Joseph, MO** is a sleeper with only 7 calls but serious money: Newtron, Enerfab, and The Waldinger Corp. are all hitting **$68.51/hr** on the Turney Energy Center. Small board, high urgency. Book 1 should move fast.

**LU-26 Washington, DC** posts 86 calls (462 hands) with JE Richards running multiple data center plays in Fredericksburg and Sterling, VA—up to 58-hour weeks and LOTO work requiring 1-year experience and current NFPA 70E. No rate posted, but the volume and 2-day safety commitment signal serious infrastructure build.

**LU-354 Salt Lake City, UT** shows Cache Valley Electric holding 40+ JW slots across QTS Fairfield (5-10s + Saturdays, **$46.22/hr** plus **$10 per diem**) and Facebook Eagle Mountain (**$46.22/hr** plus **$20 above scale**). Solid day-shift work with OT. Short calls available.

**LU-583 El Paso, TX** has Cupertino Electric's Santa Teresa job posting **$70/hr**—highest call on the board—for NM-licensed JWs, plus **$1,121 per week per diem** for 350+ mile moves. That's real relocation money for specialized work.

Data centers are vacuuming hands nationwide; every major local is hunting cable pullers and infrastructure wiremen.

LINEMAN.text:
**Trampin the IBEW Lineman Locals — Wednesday, September 30, 2026**

**LU-84 Newnan, GA** is running hot—17 calls, nearly 50 hands. SERVICE ELECTRIC's barehand transmission crew on Georgia Transmission Company work in SOCIAL CIRCLE is hitting **$56.8/hr** with **$150/day** per diem, Quanta cert required. Same contractor's got an **$46.8/hr** energized transmission job also in SOCIAL CIRCLE on an 11-on-3-off cycle. W2 ENERGY SERVICES' reconduct/conversion work runs Wednesday-Wednesday hitch, 8-on-6-off at **$46.8/hr**. If you've got the quals and the hunger, this board is moving hands fast.

**LU-1393 Indianapolis, IN** is punching above its weight at 9 calls, 13 hands. P&G Power's Goshen lineman job pays **$67.18/hr**—the board's top dog—plus **$100/day** per diem on 69kv with 12kv underbuild pole sets and wire pulls. Michels has a transmission gig in Fort Wayne at **$56.66/hr** with **$150/day** per diem on 13.2kv built work. This isn't a massive board, but the rate sheet is solid.

**LU-245 Toledo, OH** has 5 calls chasing 13 hands across transmission and distribution. DIDADO dominates with two calls at **$58.03/hr**—OAK HARBOR and SANDUSKY both running **$225/day** per diem on CDL-A work. High per diem on a transmission board means storm money or extended gear-up.

**LU-66 Houston, TX** shows 9 calls, 40 hands ready to roll, but the board posted with no rate data—all nine calls are blank on pay. NHPL's overhead distro and topped-out transmission tech work spans Houston and Floresville with **$175 per diem** on the transmission side and Class A CDL mandatory across the board. No rate visibility is unusual; dispatch may be holding scale until assignment.

**LU-17 Southfield, MI** has just 3 calls for 16 hands, all posting **$58.97/hr**. Lecom's Trumbull/Wixom distribution work and OHL's Detroit/Monroe streetlights both offer **$100/day** per diem for travelers. Thayer's Wixom distribution requires CDL-A and pays the same rate.

**LU-1426 Grand Forks, ND** anchors a cold-weather push: 4 calls, 13 hands. Parsons Electric's Polaris Forge Data Center build in Harwood runs 6-on-10s at **$44.8/hr**, **$100/day** non-taxed plus **$150 Sat/Sun** incentive for 100+ mile radius travel.

**The board is tilting toward transmission and data-center infrastructure work in the South and Midwest; tropical season and grid hardening are pulling hands.**

UA.text:
**Trampin the UA Locals — Wednesday, September 30, 2026**

**LU-776 Lima, OH** is running hot with 7 calls across 44 hands—the board's biggest play right now. Gem's got 10 combo welders headed to the fab shop (7-10s, will test you); Graham needs 4 pipefitters on Cenovus maintenance work (6-10s, spotty OT); Nooter's pushing 5 more pipefitters into the Cenovus fab shop with **$125/day** per diem and incentive pay, but you're getting current in DISA first. The other Gem call (BDO fab shop, 2 fitters, 7-10s) requires current status upfront. This is steady industrial maintenance and fab work—the kind that sticks around.

**LU-208 Denver, CO** has 5 calls, 20 hands available. The standout: Kiewit's posting 1 CWI slot at **$65** per diem (also **$65** base mentioned), night shift with **15% shift differential**, 5/10s schedule. Power Source Services wants 5 combo welders with rigging cert or rigging experience for JM Shafer Station in Fort Lupton. US Eng. Metalworks needs 2 fitters with SS fitting experience on night shift shop work. Trautman and Shreve's fab shop (3 combo welders, MIG/TIG focus) splits day and swing. Strong specialized work.

**LU-213 St John, NB** is thin—2 calls, 3 hands total—but strategic. Stuart Olson's Irving Oil Refinery call wants F3/F4 welders who can test F3/F4, starting ASAP at 7:30pm. The other call is a journeyman pipefitter into Lorneville LNG (4x10s plus, Industrial Agreement rate). Refinery and LNG infrastructure: good hold if you clear the testing.

**LU-192 Cheyenne, WY** has 1 call for 2 hands: PMI's Fort Meade VA Hospital job in Sturgis, South Dakota needs a plumber with med gas, OSHA10, and background clearance. **$100/day** per diem for days worked. Federal work, solid.

**LU-325 Fredericton, NB** shows 1 call: HVAC Inc.'s Moncton Fisheries Science Building needs a journeyman plumber, day shift (7 a.m.), 5-8s. Light board, tight timeline.

The industrial refinery and fab work is pulling hands east and south; LNG and power infrastructure keeps the momentum west.
